option.DisplayText: The Thousand and First: settlers arrive at claimed zones over time
The Thousand and First: settlements consume water and food, and can wither or famish without them
The Thousand and First: provoked factions may raid your settlements
The Thousand and First: trade charters bring caravans to your settlements
The Thousand and First: record settlement history as journal accomplishments
The Thousand and First: settlers petition you about the settlement's needs
The Thousand and First: settlements make and store power at the works you commission
The Thousand and First: the city's life is told - weddings, funerals, festivals, and breakdowns
The Thousand and First: pre-thaw and catch up your city's neighbouring zones as you move through it (experimental)
The Thousand and First: the settlement remembers its dead and names an elder among its settlers
The Thousand and First: write diagnostic lines to Player.log (dev builds)
The Thousand and First: the gathering bench gets a keeper, and travelers may pass through
The Thousand and First: designs can want a district, a larger realm, a recipe your keepers know, or more craft than the settlement has
The Thousand and First: the settlement betters its own works out of what the stores can spare
The Thousand and First: your cities take on the creeds of their settlers, and can fall out over them
The Thousand and First: staked plans are described in prose, raisings are a small ceremony, and settling notables carry a taste and a trait
The Thousand and First: you can post a price at the heart, and settlers decide for themselves whether to take it
The Thousand and First: the ground your settlers walk wears into paths, which you may pave
The Thousand and First: notable travellers arrive with a hook to chase, and may be lodged into the settlement
The Thousand and First: a planted carry-sign hauls a marked pile or container home over distance and days
The Thousand and First: settlers are assigned to specific homes, join only where one would take them, and leave if none will
The Thousand and First: consecrated shrines slowly draw neutral settlers toward their creed, and staffed scriptoria soften the ambient grudge
The Thousand and First: a settlement standing above what its works carry settles back toward them, and its works fall into disrepair
The Thousand and First: raids, hard running, and temperamental salvage can wear your works, which mend on their own out of what the stores can spare
The Thousand and First: let other mods extend your city's model through the published contract (data merges are unaffected)
The Thousand and First: your own settlers will share water with you, on Qud's own terms
